description: Labelled synthetic attribution cases used to calibrate the AETHER likelihood-ratio table. Each case mirrors a published de-anonymisation vector observed in real darknet threat-actor reporting. No real subject identifiers are used.
notes: signal values are graded indicator strengths in [0, 1]; stances default to 'supports' unless listed in stances.

cases.rationale: Apache /server-status on a clearnet origin directly links the operator's exit relay to the extortion wallet. Deterministic, high-quality.
A single self-signed TLS leaf certificate served by two unrelated darknet markets is a near-unique operator artefact.
Multi-input peel chain converges on a wallet that also appears in a prior extortion note.
All four indicator families agree: PGP key, origin leak, wallet cluster, and prose style.
Onion address published in a Certificate Transparency log for an unrelated clearnet domain.
Two unrelated actors on the same bulletproof ASN. Hosting overlap alone must not attribute.
Threat notes from the same genre and vocabulary (ransom demands) score highly on cosine similarity without a shared author. This is the headline false-positive risk of naive stylometry.
Automated malware beacons produce a circadian profile. Circadian inference over automated traffic is meaningless.
Target reachable but every module failed. The engine must report inconclusive, not guess.
A single strong deterministic artefact (PGP key reuse) is enough to justify a lead, but not a definitive attribution.
Stylometry and circadian modelling both point at a different known actor while infrastructure evidence points elsewhere. The correct output is an explicit conflict, not a confident number.

raw_values.stylometry_similarity: Author profiling matches a documented false friend (actor B), not the subject.
raw_values.diurnal_consistency: Activity cluster is 11 hours from the subject's inferred trough; matches actor B instead.

cases.rationale: Matching a Tor exit node fingerprint attributes infrastructure, not a person. Deliberately included so the corpus punishes credulous infrastructure reuse.

A confirmed PGP key reuse supports attribution, but the server presents a TLS certificate that is registered to a different, documented subject. Two fully specific artefacts cannot both be true, so the engine must raise an explicit conflict rather than average them.

raw_values.tls_cert_match: Leaf certificate is registered to a different named subject with a conflicting issuance timestamp.
